finalText:
**Merge keeps the history, rebase rewrites it.**

A merge ties two branches together with one new joining commit. Both lines of work stay visible, exactly as they happened.

A rebase replays your commits on top of the other branch. You get one straight line, and your commits get new IDs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph after_merge
    m1[main] --> mc[merge commit]
    y1[your work] --> mc
  end
  subgraph after_rebase
    m2[main] --> y2[your work, copied] --> tip[tip]
  end
```

Those new IDs are the whole rule of thumb. Rebase only commits nobody else has pulled, usually your own branch before you share it. Merge anything already shared, or the new IDs break everyone else's copy.
